title: Sherpa Tensing — Descent Two: Present Simple Passive (A2)
description: The tense of rules, processes and signs — and the passive is where it does most of its work. Nobody signs a notice we empty the bins on Fridays; they…

hero.lede: The tense of rules, processes and signs — and the passive is where it does most of its work. Nobody signs a notice we empty the bins on Fridays; they write bins are emptied on Fridays, because the bins are the point and the emptier is nobody in particular.

sections.label: Descent briefing
sections.title: When to use it
sections.lead: The passive is not a different tense. It is the present simple with the doer let go — and the reason you let them go is always one of these six.

cards.head: You do not know who
cards.body: Nobody can tell you the doer, so the sentence does without one.

cards.head: The doer does not matter
cards.body: The event is the news; who did it is a footnote.

cards.head: The doer is obvious
cards.body: Saying it would be a waste of everyone's time.

cards.head: You would rather not say
cards.body: The passive is how English removes a person from a sentence.

cards.head: Putting the important thing first
cards.body: Whatever you put at the front is what the sentence is about.

cards.head: Putting the doer back with by
cards.body: When the doer is the point, it goes at the end.
cards.ex: "The accounts are audited by an outside firm."

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: the not goes after the first auxiliary

cards.head: Questions
cards.body: the first auxiliary moves to the front

cards.head: With the doer
cards.ex: "The report is written by the duty officer."

charts.head: Turning an active sentence around
charts.note: Three moves, always the same: the object comes to the front, the verb becomes am / is / are + participle, and the old subject either disappears or goes to the back behind by. Only the middle step changes from camp to camp.

head: Active
Passive
What moved
rows: They empty the bins on Fridays.
The bins are emptied on Fridays.
An outside firm audits the accounts.
The accounts are audited by an outside firm.
The firm matters, so it stayed.
Someone checks tickets at the barrier.
Tickets are checked at the barrier.

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Only be changes, exactly as it does in camp two: am, is or are. The participle never moves.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this one is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: The bins are empty on Fridays.
The bins are emptied on Fridays.
Without the participle you have written an adjective: the bins are simply not full.
English does not do the speaking. If the subject is not the doer, you need the passive.
Happen takes no object, so it has no passive at all.

charts.note: Neither is better. The question is only what the sentence is about — because whatever you put at the front is what the reader will think it is about.

head: Question
Passive
Active
rows:
The thing it happens to.
"The bins are emptied on Fridays."

The one who does it.
"They empty the bins on Fridays."
Often not — and you do not need to.
Yes, and you are naming them.
At the end with by, or nowhere at all.
At the front, as the subject.
Longer by two or three words.
Usually shorter. Prefer it when both work.

charts.example: This is the tense of every sign, manual and set of instructions you will ever read in English. Doors are closed at 6pm. Payment is taken on collection. Nobody is named, because the rule applies whoever is on duty — and that anonymity is the whole point.

sections.title: Signal words

signals.head: Verbs with no passive at all

sections.example: The test for whether a verb can go passive: does it take an object? They built it has one, so it turns. It happened has none, so it cannot.

sections.label: Interactive
sections.title: The event, and the doer you dropped

diagram.intro: The block is the same block as the ascent, lit from above instead of fading into the dark — because the tense has not changed, only the light. Inside it sits a dashed box: the doer. It is drawn inside the event rather than beside it because the doer is not a moment in time, it is a part of the sentence — and it is dashed because most of the time nobody says it. Click either to see it in a sentence.

panels.head: The doer — optional, and usually gone
items: … and usually, by nobody you need to name.

quiz.explain: Plural subject, so are, and the participle emptied. Are empty would be an adjective.

quiz.hint: The subject is not the doer.
quiz.explain: English does not speak. Speak / spoke / spoken gives the participle.
Bridge is singular, so is, and the participle inspected.

quiz.prompt: The accounts _____ by an outside firm. (audit)
quiz.explain: Accounts is plural, so are, and the doer goes at the end behind by.
The not goes after are, and the participle follows.
Is + subject + participle. Room is singular.
Happen takes no object, so there is no passive form of it.
Payment is singular, and the participle of take is taken.
Plural subject, so are, with the participle reviewed.
Doors is plural. Note that close also works actively here; the passive removes the closer.
I takes am, and the participle of pay is paid.
Made is the participle. Note that a material takes from, not by.

quiz.prompt: We _____ when a decision is reached. (tell)
quiz.explain: We is plural, and the participle of tell is told.
Is cleaned is the routine; is clean would only describe its state.

results: Clean run. You can turn a sentence around and you know when the doer is worth keeping.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at the active version before you go on.
Good first attempt. The auxiliary chain is the part to read again.
